title: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value
author: Katie Shonk, Program on Negotiation, Harvard Law School

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 1

segments.text: Both inexperienced and seasoned negotiators often assume they must choose between two approaches:

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 2

segments.text: Negotiate aggressively and take a hard-line stance, or

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 3

segments.text: Be friendly and accommodating to preserve the relationship.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 4

segments.text: In reality, there is a more effective third path—one that moves beyond toughness or accommodation and increases the likelihood of achieving meaningful, lasting results.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 5

segments.text: In Getting to Yes: Negotiating Agreement Without Giving In (2nd ed.), Roger Fisher, William Ury, and Bruce Patton of the Harvard Negotiation Project introduced principled negotiation, also known as negotiation on the merits. Their method is designed “to produce wise outcomes efficiently and amicably.”

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 6

segments.text: Rather than focusing on who wins, principled negotiation focuses on solving the problem.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 7

segments.text: The 4 Elements of Principled Negotiation

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 8

segments.text: In Getting to Yes, Fisher, Ury, and Patton outline four core elements. Mastering them can significantly improve your negotiation skills.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 9

segments.text: Separate the People from the Problem

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 10

segments.text: Strong emotions often become entangled with substantive issues. When that happens, negotiation becomes personal—and progress stalls.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 11

segments.text: Principled negotiation encourages parties to address emotional and relational concerns separately from the issues at stake.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 12

segments.text: For example, imagine two department heads locked in a heated dispute over limited budget resources. The disagreement may be fueled by deeper concerns:

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 13

segments.text: Fear of losing influence

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 14

segments.text: Pressure from senior leadership

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 15

segments.text: Anxiety about team performance

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 16

segments.text: Rather than trying to “win” the budget battle, effective negotiators would:

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 17

segments.text: Practice active listening

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 18

segments.text: Acknowledge emotions

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 19

segments.text: Clarify misunderstandings

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 20

segments.text: Reframe the issue as a joint problem

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 21

segments.text: The goal is not victory over the other party—but clarity and mutual understanding.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 22

segments.text: Focus on Interests, Not Positions

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 23

segments.text: Negotiators frequently argue over positions—fixed demands such as “We need a 10% raise” or “The party must be at my house.”

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 24

segments.text: Positions are surface-level statements. Beneath them lie interests—the underlying needs, motivations, and concerns driving those demands.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 25

segments.text: A Simple Example

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 26

segments.text: Two siblings disagree about where to host their parents’ anniversary party:

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 27

segments.text: One insists on a restaurant.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 28

segments.text: The other insists on hosting at home.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 29

segments.text: Only when they explore their interests do they make progress:

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 30

segments.text: The restaurant advocate lacks time for preparation.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 31

segments.text: The home advocate is concerned about cost.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 32

segments.text: With that understanding, they choose an affordable restaurant.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 33

segments.text: By focusing on interests instead of positions, negotiators often discover creative solutions that satisfy both sides.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 34

segments.text: This approach—sometimes called interest-based bargaining—is at the heart of principled negotiation.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 35

segments.text: Invent Options for Mutual Gain

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 36

segments.text: Negotiators often stop searching once they reach a minimally acceptable agreement. Principled negotiation encourages something different: deliberate creativity before commitment.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 37

segments.text: Instead of rushing toward compromise, parties should:

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 38

segments.text: Brainstorm multiple options

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 39

segments.text: Suspend judgment during idea generation

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 40

segments.text: Look for trades across issues

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 41

segments.text: In negotiation, “options” can include:

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 42

segments.text: Contingencies

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 43

segments.text: Conditions

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 44

segments.text: Timing adjustments

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 45

segments.text: Performance incentives

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 46

segments.text: Issue trades

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 47

segments.text: Example: A Job Negotiation

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 48

segments.text: Suppose:

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 49

segments.text: The candidate prioritizes higher salary.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 50

segments.text: The organization prioritizes staffing continuity and budget discipline.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 51

segments.text: Possible mutual-gain options might include:

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 52

segments.text: Reduced vacation days in exchange for higher base pay

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 53

segments.text: Performance-based bonuses

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 54

segments.text: A signing bonus instead of a salary increase

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 55

segments.text: A future salary review tied to measurable milestones

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 56

segments.text: By expanding the conversation beyond a single issue, negotiators create more value before dividing it.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 57

segments.text: Insist on Objective Criteria

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 58

segments.text: Many negotiations devolve into debates over whose “facts” are correct. That path often leads to impasse or arbitrary compromise.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 59

segments.text: Principled negotiation recommends grounding decisions in objective criteria—fair, independent standards that both sides agree to use.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 60

segments.text: Examples of objective criteria include:

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 61

segments.text: Market value

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 62

segments.text: Industry benchmarks

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 63

segments.text: Expert opinion

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 64

segments.text: Legal standards

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 65

segments.text: Professional norms

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 66

segments.text: The key is mutual agreement in advance about which standards will apply.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 67

segments.text: For example, in a salary negotiation, both parties might agree to rely on published compensation data from reputable industry sources. This reduces personal friction and reframes the discussion as a shared search for fairness.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 68

segments.text: Don’t Forget Your BATNA

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 69

segments.text: A common misconception about principled negotiation is that the goal is simply to reach agreement.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 70

segments.text: It is not.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 71

segments.text: The goal is to reach an agreement that is better than your BATNA—your Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 72

segments.text: According to Getting to Yes, understanding and strengthening your BATNA is critical.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 73

segments.text: Before and during negotiation, ask:

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 74

segments.text: What will I do if this deal fails?

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 75

segments.text: How strong is my alternative?

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 76

segments.text: How can I improve it?

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 77

segments.text: For example, a homebuyer negotiating on multiple properties strengthens their BATNA by maintaining credible alternatives. A job candidate interviewing at multiple firms does the same.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 78

segments.text: The stronger your BATNA, the more confidently you can negotiate—and the more comfortable you can be walking away from an inferior deal.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 79

segments.text: If, after exploring interests and options, an agreement does not exceed your BATNA, walking away is not a failure. It is disciplined decision-making.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 80

segments.text: Why Principled Negotiation Works

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 81

segments.text: Principled negotiation works because it:

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 82

segments.text: Reduces emotional escalation

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 83

segments.text: Encourages collaborative problem solving

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 84

segments.text: Expands the pool of potential value

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 85

segments.text: Grounds decisions in fairness and legitimacy

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 86

segments.text: Protects you from agreeing to a bad deal

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 87

segments.text: It replaces the false choice between hard bargaining and accommodation with a structured, strategic approach.

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 88

segments.text: What Has Been Your Experience?

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 89

segments.text: Have you used principled negotiation in your own professional or personal negotiations?

locator.section: Principled Negotiation: Focus on Interests to Create Value, article block 90

segments.text: What challenges have you faced when separating people from the problem—or insisting on objective criteria?
